name: alert
description: Inline feedback banners for system-level messages. Three variants: Default (neutral), Destructive (error), Warning (caution). Non-blocking — does not steal focus or require a decision.

gaps.note: Layout structure differs by variant combination. Two layouts exist.

flatLayout.structure: title and description are direct children of the alert frame

nestedLayout.structure: icon + content frame + action-slot are siblings inside the alert frame

alert.flatLayout: Has Icon=False AND Has Action=False — title + description are direct children of alert frame, no content wrapper
alert.nestedLayout: Has Icon=True OR Has Action=True — icon (optional) + content frame (title + description) + action-slot (optional) are siblings
alert.actionSlot: Named FRAME instance, typed to Button only, shown/hidden by Has Action boolean prop

accessibility.role: alert for inline banner; alertdialog for modal dialog
accessibility.focusManagement: Alert dialog traps focus and moves focus to first focusable element on open.
keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab cycle footer buttons

constraints: Use inline alert for non-blocking feedback.
Use alert-dialog only when user must acknowledge or decide.
Warning variant intentionally uses primitive yellow tokens (color/yellow/*) — design decision, not a bug.
Do not override button fills inside action-slot.
Alert-dialog Type=Destructive must include a cancel path.

useCases: Displaying a form submission error inline below the form header so the user sees it without scrolling
Warning a user that their free trial expires in 3 days — a persistent banner they should read but don't have to act on immediately
Confirming a destructive action (deleting a workspace) with a modal alert-dialog before it executes
Announcing a new feature or policy change at the top of a settings page
Surfacing an async error after a failed save, inline in the affected section
Blocking the user from proceeding until they acknowledge a critical configuration problem (alert-dialog)

Default.whenToUse: Neutral information, success confirmation, or a general announcement

Destructive.whenToUse: Validation failure, API error, or confirmation that something irreversible occurred
examples: Payment failed — check your card details.
Could not delete project — try again.

Warning.whenToUse: Caution state where action is optional but advisable
examples: Your API key expires in 7 days.
This action affects all team members.

comparedTo.situation: Feedback that auto-dismisses after a completed action (save, copy, send)
comparedTo.notInstead: alert (alert is persistent; toast is transient)

comparedTo.situation: The page has loaded but there is simply no data to show
comparedTo.notInstead: alert (alert signals something wrong or noteworthy, not an empty state)

comparedTo.situation: User must make a choice before continuing — both buttons are real decisions (delete, revoke, overwrite)
comparedTo.notInstead: dialog — dialog has a neutral close (× button), alertdialog forces a choice

comparedTo.situation: User needs a modal for a form, review, or complex content — can dismiss neutrally with ×
comparedTo.notInstead: alert-dialog — alertdialog should not have a neutral close on destructive actions

comparedTo.situation: Inline validation error on a single form field
comparedTo.notInstead: alert (alert is for section- or page-level messages, not per-field errors)

bestPractice.decisionGuide: See Alert.md — Alert vs AlertDialog vs Dialog Decision Guide section. Key rule: if both buttons are real choices (cancel ≠ close), use alertdialog. If user can exit neutrally (× = valid outcome), use dialog. If no blocking needed, use inline alert.

notes: Warning variant primitive tokens (color/yellow/*) are intentional — accepted design decision 2026-05-28.

Alert-dialog footer button fills are intentional — the parent component sets the root fill on each button instance (primary/outline/destructive). This is required because Figma API fills=[] removes the visual color; these fills must be kept.
action-slot stays as BOOLEAN-controlled FRAME (buttons only) — no native SLOT conversion. Decided 2026-05-28.
AlertDialog has been separated into its own file: alert-dialog.meta.json

darkMode.notes: No known dark mode differences — all tokens are semantic and mode-aware.

storybook.title: Feedback/Alert
storybook.notes: Alert-only stories. AlertDialog has its own separate story file and meta.json.

relatedComponents.name: alert-dialog
relatedComponents.reason: AlertDialog is the modal version requiring an explicit decision. Alert is inline and non-blocking.

relatedComponents.name: toast
relatedComponents.reason: Toast auto-dismisses after an action; Alert is persistent until dismissed.

relatedComponents.name: empty
relatedComponents.reason: Empty is for no-data states; Alert signals something wrong or noteworthy.
